solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flourish as learner in time of prosperity

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic growth
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student blossoms during good economic times.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to blossom or thrive, a straight synonym of flourish as a verb.

clue.text: Smear second-rate group

parts.note: B grade is second-rate, below A
a lot is a group or batch of things

explanation.surface: A slur against some inferior band or set of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain or mark, so it is a synonym of smear as a noun.

clue.text: Exclamation of love, repeated with afterthought

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, and it is written twice
PS, postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A letter-writer repeats a loving cry and then adds a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is a cry uttered on making a small mistake, an example of an exclamation.

clue.text: Devious importers giving false account

indicators.note: devious means crooked or winding, so the letters take a twisted route into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shady importers lie about what they brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: A misreport is an inaccurate report, so it is an untrue account of events.

clue.text: Criticise star with a "wonder cure"

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
an ace is a star performer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a celebrity who endorses a miracle remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for all ills, which is what a miracle cure promises.

clue.text: Person shunned in French city endlessly, a husband

indicators.note: without an end means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the French capital
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A married man is ostracised in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is an outcast whom others avoid, so a social reject.

clue.text: Head is crazy person

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for the skull or head
second meaning: slang for a madman

explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech the word means both the head and a lunatic or fanatic.

clue.text: Extremely robust, a prison? Prisoner gets outside it!

indicators.note: getting outside something means wrapping round it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
taken as written
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail seems very secure, yet an inmate escapes it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' points back to 'a prison', which the convict goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron as an adjective means unbreakable or firm, as in a cast-iron guarantee.

clue.text: Claim Yorkshire town has no hotel

indicators.note: having none of something means that letter is taken out

parts.note: a spa town in North Yorkshire
Hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A northern town complains it lacks a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or claim something without right, so a verb for claiming.

clue.text: Propose changes? Voter not in favour

indicators.note: changes asks for the order of these letters to be altered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tables amendments and another member votes against.
explanation.definitionFit: An opposer is one who opposes, such as a voter against a motion.

clue.text: What a serial! Characters in it provide a shocker

indicators.note: some of the letters inside the preceding words form the solution

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A viewer exclaims at a TV serial whose characters deliver a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like the cast of the serial; it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock weapon, so literally a device that delivers a shock.

clue.text: Punishing writer and boxer, I perform song

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion
what someone says when performing a song: I sing

explanation.surface: An author, a fighter and a singer form an odd act.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalising someone is imposing a penalty, so it is a form of punishing.

clue.text: One politician finishing on the way

parts.note: Roman numeral one
Member of Parliament
ending means finishing

explanation.surface: A lone MP wraps up a career and is on the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending is about to happen, so it is coming, approaching soon.

clue.text: Two cricket sides making irregular appearances?

wordplay.note: the off side and the on side are the two halves of a cricket field, either side of the batsman

explanation.surface: Two cricket teams turn up only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side; 'sides' looks like teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Off and on means intermittently, so something that comes and goes at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Exact account given by junior minister

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A precise report delivered by a lower-ranking government member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests government, but here it is a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct in every detail, a synonym of exact as an adjective.

clue.text: Female performer gets agent

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an actor is a stage performer

explanation.surface: An actress signs up with a theatrical agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' seems like a showbiz representative; a factor is a business agent who acts for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is someone who buys and sells on behalf of another, a mercantile agent.

clue.text: Work with solicitor or choose to depart?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tout solicits custom, not a lawyer here

explanation.surface: Someone weighs staying with a law firm or resigning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a British lawyer; here it is one who solicits trade, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to decide to withdraw from an arrangement, so to elect to leave.

clue.text: Like a manned boat sounding primitive

indicators.note: sounding means the solution is said like a word for the next idea

parts.note: crude means rough or primitive

explanation.surface: A rough, basic craft with sailors aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A crewed boat has a crew aboard, which is what manned means for a vessel.

clue.text: Grown-up to speak furiously, having swallowed drug (impure stuff)

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so the pair of words takes in another

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
E is slang for ecstasy
to rant is to speak angrily

explanation.surface: An adult on drugs shouting angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words are the definition, set off from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance added that makes something impure, such as a cutting agent.

clue.text: Member to ascend without leader

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to climb is to go up

explanation.surface: A club member seeks to rise with no one at the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a member of a party; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb, an arm or leg, is a member of the body in the old anatomical sense.

clue.text: Not in favour of a drink with tonic?

parts.note: taken as written
gin is the spirit drunk with tonic

explanation.surface: Someone declines a gin and tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, meaning opposed to something.

clue.text: Doctor and a mother in play

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A medic and a mum appear as characters in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a piece written for performance, a synonym of play as a noun.

clue.text: Tool making holes everyone heard

indicators.note: heard means we take the spoken version of the word

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone hears a drill boring holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed hand tool used for piercing leather or wood.

clue.text: Excellent time in side anticipating action?

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the next word

parts.note: a wing is a side of a building, team or army
A1 means excellent, written with I for 1
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A top-notch moment for a team's flank as it waits for the play.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 becomes AI because the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting means expecting something to happen, so the solver is in a state of anticipation.

clue.text: Want a source of light, becoming angry

parts.note: to want is to need
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a source of light

explanation.surface: Someone lacking a lamp grows cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means irritated or provoked, so annoyed and angry.

clue.text: Continue to chatter in the country

parts.note: gab is idle talk
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: People in rural parts keep on gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like the countryside; it names a nation. Gab on is a phrase for continuing to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the west coast of Central Africa.
